An incomplete cast copper alloy enamelled zoomorphic plate brooch in the shape of a sitting cockerel of Roman date (AD 100-250). The brooch is piriform in plan, rounded at the front and slightly pointed at the back with a domed upper surface and hollow concave reverse. The zoomorphic / cockerel features consist of a head which extends from the rounded end and a tail emanating from the pointed end. The head is flat and sub-circular in profile; the comb extends above but is lost due to abrasion; the beak is similarly lost. The eyes (one on either side of the head) are made from a drilled ring-and-dot motif; it is possible that the centre of the eye had a red enamel inlay - now lost. The tail…
